canonical_statement: For every real-valued discrete-time martingale X on a probability space, deterministic nonnegative bounds c, horizon n, and t >= 0, if |X_(k+1)-X_k| <= c_(k+1) almost surely for every k < n, then P(t <= X_n-X_0) <= exp(-t^2/(2 sum_{j=1}^n c_j^2)).
domain_and_universes: Omega : Type u; probability measure mu; filtration indexed by Nat; X : Nat -> Omega -> Real; c : Nat -> NNReal; n : Nat; t : Real
ordered_binders: for every k < n, the step-k increment is a.e. absolutely bounded by c (k+1)
conclusion: mu.real {omega | t <= X n omega - X 0 omega} <= Real.exp (-(t^2) / (2 * sum_{k in range n} (c (k+1))^2))
index_convention: Times are 0,...,n; range n indexes the n increments by k+1, so the denominator is sum_{j=1}^n c_j^2.
boundary_convention: n=0, t=0, and zero squared-bound sum remain in the target and use Lean's total real division; no positivity assumption on the denominator is added.
